title: Unit – 4 : Session – 10 : SLO – 1  |  B Trees
sections: A B Tree is a SELF-BALANCING (m-way search) tree.
B Trees are used in DATABASES and FILE SYSTEMS.
A B Tree of order m has at most m CHILDREN.
A node can contain at most m-1 keys.
All leaf nodes appear on the SAME LEVEL.
Internal nodes have at least ceil(m/2) children.
B Trees grow and shrink from the ROOT (top).
Insertion in B Trees is done at the LEAF LEVEL.
If a node overflows, it is SPLIT.
If a node underflows, it may MERGE or REDISTRIBUTE (borrow).
B Trees eliminate the need for REORGANIZATION (rebalancing of the whole tree) after insertions and deletions.
B Trees reduce time for DISK (secondary storage) accesses.
B Trees are generalizations of BINARY SEARCH TREES (2-3 trees).
